title: Marvel Movies That May Have Foreshadowed Doctor Doom's MCU Arrival
excerpt:
A new analysis links several Marvel film scenes to Avengers: Doomsday.
Many proposed connections remain interpretation rather than confirmed story details.
body_md:
As the Marvel Cinematic Universe moves toward Avengers: Doomsday, fans are debating whether Victor von Doom's arrival was carefully prepared or whether the character was introduced as a late replacement for an earlier central antagonist. A new retrospective identifies moments in several Marvel films that could connect to the upcoming multiversal storyline. The key distinction is that some of these scenes are established on-screen events, while their connection to Doom remains speculative.

The Marvels provides one potential starting point. Its ending strands Monica Rambeau in another universe, where she encounters an alternate version of her mother and Beast, voiced by Kelsey Grammer. The sequence clearly broadens the franchise's connection to X-Men characters and alternate realities. The article proposes that this displacement might contribute to a future multiversal crisis, but Monica's involvement in Doomsday and the exact mechanism of such a crisis are not confirmed by that scene.

Captain America: Brave New World offers another possible link. Sam Wilson moves toward assembling a new Avengers team, while the Leader warns him in a post-credits scene about a threat involving other universes. That warning is compatible with the kind of conflict associated with Doom in the article's interpretation. It does not, however, explicitly identify Doom as the subject of the warning, so the connection should not be presented as established fact.

Thunderbolts* supplies a more visible bridge between superhero groups. Its post-credits sequence shows the New Avengers encountering evidence of a multiversal event, including the arrival of a spacecraft associated with the Fantastic Four. This provides a plausible narrative connection between the teams. It does not independently establish who is aboard the vessel or the full circumstances of its journey.

The Fantastic Four: First Steps contains the most direct connection discussed in the retrospective. A mid-credits sequence involving Franklin Richards points toward Doctor Doom himself. The article suggests that Franklin's unusual powers could be important to Doom's interests and the events of Doomsday. Even with a more explicit character connection, the precise motives and consequences are matters for the films' story to establish.

The writer also discusses purported material in an Encore version of Avengers: Endgame involving Loki, Steve Rogers, Bruce Banner and the Time Variance Authority. Those claims appear in the source article, but should not be treated as independently verified plot facts without additional confirmation. Theories about Steve's time travel causing an incursion or Doom gathering powerful heroes similarly remain theories rather than announced narrative details.

Taken together, these films establish a broad network of multiverse storylines, X-Men connections, Fantastic Four developments and evolving Avengers teams. Whether every element was originally designed to lead to Doctor Doom is a separate question. The most useful way to read the retrospective is as a map of possible narrative connections, with a clear line between what the audience has seen and what commentators expect may happen next.
seo_title: Which Marvel Movies Set Up Doctor Doom?
seo_description: A careful look at possible Doctor Doom clues in The Marvels, Brave New World, Thunderbolts and Fantastic Four, separating facts from theories.
